title: Concerning Criticism
author: No-Marionberry-772
selftext:
There is a fine line between criticism and insults that people are very bad at walking in general. People are also bad at recognizing when others cross that line. Some people, usually people who have suffered from oversensitivity, can see it very easily and know how to walk it.

That is the problem with criticism: it asks you to walk right up to that line. The moment you cross the line, you ruin the criticism and it won't be received.

I cannot know the context of the specific issues, but constructive criticism doesn't involve comments unrelated to the specific issue.

If the art is individually good but seems to not hold to a common theme, don't just say that. Point out specific things:
"The chair models would work better with the tables if their legs had the same profile."

Constructive criticism includes specific suggestions. It's not only pointing out problems; it's suggesting possible solutions to help get the creative process moving.

Without the suggestions, it's called complaining.

Please do better, when you have input to someones project, make sure you have a view on how it can be improved, not just what you dislike about it.
